subject.title: fix(secrets): surface degradation in logs and doctor

question: Should known webhook-route SecretRef failures be isolated as cold owners during startup and reload, instead of retaining the prior route behavior, with public requests continuing to receive generic unauthorized responses?
rationale: This is a deliberate security and compatibility boundary change for existing webhook deployments, and the protected maintainer label requires human confirmation even if the implementation is technically sound.

options.title: Confirm route isolation after exact-head proof
options.body: Approve owner-scoped webhook-route isolation once a redacted current-head Gateway run proves the route remains generic externally and diagnostics contain no SecretRef identity.

options.title: Keep webhook routes fail-closed
options.body: Limit this PR to observability for existing isolated owners and defer webhook-route isolation until its operational policy is separately approved.

options.title: Adopt a narrower route policy
options.body: Define which webhook route classes may isolate and require the implementation and tests to enforce that explicit boundary.

recommendation.title: Confirm route isolation after exact-head proof
recommendation.body: Approve owner-scoped webhook-route isolation once a redacted current-head Gateway run proves the route remains generic externally and diagnostics contain no SecretRef identity.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the merged owner-scoped SecretRef isolation model that defines the boundary this PR expands.
